items.title: [leparisien.fr] WMO says powerful El Niño likely to persist through February 2027
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) says the strong El Niño developing in the tropical Pacific is expected to peak in December and is nearly certain to persist until February 2027. The climate pattern, which warms the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, is forecast to bring above-average temperatures across much of the world and shift rainfall patterns, increasing drought and flood risks in different regions. In Ecuador, the Navy’s Oceanographic and Antarctic Institute reported sea temperatures as much as 5.2°C above normal off Ecuador and Peru. It linked the unusually warm water to exceptional coastal rainfall, rainfall deficits in the Andean highlands and Amazon, and reduced nutrient levels affecting some fisheries. Officials urged preparations for coastal flooding. Separately, Copernicus reported that the global average sea-surface temperature outside polar regions reached a September record of 21.05°C.

items.title: [cnbc.com] Meta lifts AI spending plan as $825 billion commitments unsettle investors
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

Meta Platforms shares fell nearly 7% on Thursday, Oct. 22, after the company raised the lower end of its 2026 capital-spending forecast by $5 billion and reported negative quarterly free cash flow for the first time in more than a decade. Meta also disclosed about $825 billion in future lease and contract commitments tied largely to its AI infrastructure buildout. Third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, beating analysts’ expectations, but free cash flow was negative $2.12 billion as spending increased. Meta said it plans to create nonvoting Class C shares to give it more flexibility to finance growth; it has said it could raise hundreds of billions of dollars over several years through share issuances. The selloff extended beyond Meta: the Nasdaq fell 2.6%, the S&P 500 lost 1.2% and the Philadelphia semiconductor index dropped about 6.7% on Thursday. Meta’s new share class is scheduled to take effect on Jan. 19, 2027, under the company’s plan.

items.title: [farmer.pl] Farmers urged to shred corn stalks to curb pests and disease
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

As Poland’s corn harvest continues, agronomic guidance recommends finely shredding stalks and other crop residues after harvest to reduce winter shelter for the European corn borer and limit disease in the next season. The borer’s larvae overwinter in stalks, while feeding damage can promote Fusarium infections that contaminate grain with mycotoxins. Residue management also affects soil organic matter: grain corn leaves substantial biomass in the field, while silage harvesting removes nearly all above-ground material. Guidance recommends accounting for soil moisture and the next crop; working wet soil can cause compaction, and fields vulnerable to erosion may need residue left on the surface.
